title: Dholavira adapts a city to scarce water
summary: At Dholavira in present-day Gujarat, a Harappan community developed reservoirs, fortified districts and craft workshops. The city’s water management responded to a dry environment supplied by seasonal streams.

claims.text: At Dholavira in present-day Gujarat, a Harappan community developed reservoirs, fortified districts and craft workshops. The city’s water management responded to a dry environment supplied by seasonal streams.
Occupation range for this city, not the duration of the entire Indus civilization.

Water infrastructure offers a way to compare urban communities beyond rulers and battles. The archaeological site also preserves evidence of trade with other Harappan cities, Mesopotamia and the Oman peninsula.
